Capture, offline analysis and deauthentication frame analysis are read-only diagnostics. The modules of the attack workbench actively put frames on the air or make clients re-handshake, which can disrupt other people\u2019s networks; make sure you hold the network owner\u2019s explicit authorisation first.

tcpdump (packaged with the ARM64 build) handles passive capture and offline filtering and is unpacked into app-private storage at runtime. aireplay-ng, aircrack-ng, airodump-ng, hostapd and friends are detected in the device environment; missing ones are reported as missing and never pretended to be bundled.

Sends deauthentication and disassociation frames to the target access point so that connected clients are forced offline or have to re-handshake.
Keeps broadcasting forged beacon frames to disturb the access point selection of the clients.
Sends forged authentication requests to try to fill the connection table of the access point.
Listens to the target access point and stores the WPA/WPA2 four-way handshake for a later offline verification.
Verifies a captured handshake against a wordlist without any radio activity.
Uses hostapd to broadcast an access point with the same name as the target and evaluates how the clients pick an access point.
ARP spoofing / man in the middle
Performs ARP spoofing against a chosen client so that forwarded traffic can be observed. The module works on the data interface and needs no monitor interface.

Wireless interface, mode and channel management
Discovers the wireless interfaces and the channels published by the driver. A passive capture can be stored as a PCAP with at most 50,000 frames and 512 bytes per frame.
Monitoring is normally passive, but changing the channel may disconnect the current Wi-Fi. Only test devices you own or are authorised to test.
\nThe channel list comes from iw list; whether an interface can be created and tuned still depends on the driver.
